minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard sewer, Monty Tech and general government budgets, then planned an April 1 remote meeting on its report.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the town manager's update on trash and natural gas contracts, then the Sewer Commission's budget and rate increase, Monty Tech's budget and Chapter 70 explanation, and the finance director's general government, health insurance and debt presentation. Long discussion followed on debt capacity, a Proposition 2.5 override, and what the committee's annual report to town meeting should contain. It voted to schedule a remote April 1 meeting solely on the report and adjourned near 11:30 pm.

public_comment.topic: Argued that town positions such as the senior center cook should not be scrutinized like private-sector roles, citing per-pupil spending versus tax bills compared to Wayland.

votes.motion: Request the chair to schedule a meeting for April 1st as a placeholder, remote, solely to review and revise the committee's report.

budget_items.what_was_said: New three-year locked rate for town and school natural gas from November 2025, higher than the current rate.

budget_items.topic: Solid waste and recycling contract extension
budget_items.what_was_said: Hauler wanted an increase to extend because routes take more labor hours than bid; town will rebid and explore a cart/tote system, with bag fees offsetting disposal costs.
Town manager said a subscription service would cost residents far more than the current system.
The Sewer Commission was awarded ARPA funds to repair manholes contributing to inflow and infiltration.

budget_items.topic: Unplanned forcemain repair at Mass One
budget_items.what_was_said: Emergency repair of a corroded coupling was completed.
Rate rising due to Fitchburg and Leominster increases and infrastructure needs; minimum quarterly charge and connection fee also rising.
Presented projected revenue lines including connection fees, permit fees, investment income and betterments.
Expenses total reported; retained earnings appropriation needed to cover the difference and emergency buffer.

budget_items.topic: Sewer possible grant funding for pumps
budget_items.what_was_said: Commission hopes for grant funding through Green Communities to reduce pump costs.
Monty Tech listed workforce, equipment and Perkins grants it has won this year.

budget_items.topic: Monty Tech Foundation budget and Chapter 70
budget_items.what_was_said: Monty Tech is a hold harmless district receiving minimum aid; low-income group change reduced foundation budget.
Transportation, capital, stabilization transfers and use of excess and deficiency to reduce assessments.
Salary, transportation and technology/cyber security drive the increase.
Lunenburg's required minimum and proposed assessment rise, driven by enrollment and wealth factors.
Collective bargaining raises of three to four percent; transportation bid first-year increase double digits.
Finance director walked through small line increases, with salaries pending the salary administration plan article.
New 19-hour clerk position proposed; principal assessor line rising with new hire.
New line for outsourced grant writing; procurement threshold discussed.
Nashoba health district assessment up.
Actual renewal lower than target; history of renewal rates and stabilization fund draw discussed.
Insurance estimates rise; salary and reserve fund estimates decrease from FY24 levels.
Debt service falling as some debt retires; total and funding sources by exempt, enterprise and MSBA.

budget_items.topic: ARPA reallocation and pavement management pause
budget_items.what_was_said: Select board reallocated ARPA to school items; town manager will pause pavement management increase to shift funds toward schools.
Committee discussed expected Fair Share revenue for Chapter 90.

transfers.description: Draw from health insurance stabilization fund to supplement health insurance cost last year; remainder to be used this year.
Possible move of money out of Chapter 90 to cover pause of pavement management increase if needed.

decisions.decision: Chair will post an April 1 7 pm remote meeting limited to one agenda item, review and revision of the committee's report, cancelling if no draft is ready.
A short meeting will be scheduled for April 4 for the report and any warrant articles not finished on the 28th.
Public hearing on March 28 will start at 6:30 with a possible omnibus budget presentation, recessing the hearing as needed.
Chair will send a revised agenda placing the five sets of minutes at the front of the next night's meeting.
The report will include a factual table or graph of override impact by house value, stating the increase is permanent; no persuasion.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted to ask the chair to schedule a remote April 1 meeting solely to review and revise its report; one member was heard opposed.
The chair will post the April 1 7 pm meeting with one agenda item and cancel it if no draft is ready; a short April 4 meeting is also planned.
The committee agreed its report will include a factual table or graph of the override's effect by house value, stating the increase is permanent.
The Sewer Commission presented its FY25 enterprise budget and a sewer rate increase effective July 1, 2024, citing higher Fitchburg and Leominster charges and infrastructure needs.
The town manager reported a new three-year natural gas rate higher than the current one, and a trash contract extension the hauler priced higher, which the town will rebid.

why_it_matters: The sewer rate increase effective July 1, 2024 and a higher natural gas rate from November 2025 touch resident sewer bills and town and school operating costs.
The trash contract will be rebid, possibly with a cart system and bag fees, which could change how residents pay for and set out trash.
The committee's report to town meeting, including the override impact by house value, is what voters will read before a Proposition 2.5 override vote.
watch_next: April 1, 7 pm remote meeting on the committee's report, cancelled if no draft is ready; a short April 4 meeting for the report and unfinished warrant articles.
March 28 public hearing at 6:30 pm, with a possible omnibus budget presentation.
